departments.name: Political Council (Политический совет)
departments.description: The collective governing body of 19 members that directs all party activities. The party has no single leader—all decisions are made collegially. A presidium can be elected from within the council for specific matters.

departments.name: Executive Committee (Исполнительный комитет)
departments.description: Executive body responsible for day-to-day party operations. Headed by Dosaly Esenaliev from January 2014.

departments.name: Youth Committee (Молодёжный комитет)
departments.description: Youth wing organization of the party.

departments.name: Presidium (Президиум)
departments.description: A subset of the Political Council elected to handle specific operational decisions.

recent_events.title: Party Founded as Liberal Democratic Party
recent_events.description: Founded at the constituent congress on 28 June 2010 and registered as the 'Liberal Democratic Party Bir Bol'. Altynbek Sulaymanov and Emilbek Kaptagaev were among the key founders.
recent_events.impact: Established a new liberal political force in Kyrgyzstan following the 2010 revolution.

recent_events.title: II Congress and Name Change
recent_events.description: At the II congress on 16 November 2013, the party changed its name to 'Bir Bol—Political Party of State Unity and Patriotism' and adopted its strategic platform and charter. Ideological platform presented by historian Kiyas Moldokasymov.
recent_events.impact: Rebranded party identity centered on patriotism and state unity principles.

recent_events.title: Entered Parliament with 12 Seats
recent_events.description: In the 2015 Kyrgyz parliamentary election, Bir Bol garnered 8.52% of the vote (8.4% per Russian Wikipedia), winning 12 seats in the Supreme Council (Jogorku Kenesh) and entering parliament for the first time.
recent_events.impact: Became a parliamentary party; initially joined the opposition.

recent_events.title: Joined Ruling Majority Coalition
recent_events.description: On 3 November 2016, Bir Bol together with SDPK and Kyrgyzstan party formed the Majority Coalition, which nominated candidates for government positions and received approval from President Almazbek Atambaev.
recent_events.impact: Shifted from opposition to pro-government coalition; gained influence in government formation.

recent_events.title: Bir Bol Representative Elected First Vice PM
recent_events.description: In December 2017, Bir Bol representative Askarbek Shadiev was elected First Vice Prime Minister after the Majority Coalition proposed Dastanbek Dzhumabekov for parliament speaker (approved by 80 deputies).
recent_events.impact: Party gained a senior executive government position.

recent_events.title: Lost All Parliamentary Seats in 2020 Election
recent_events.description: In the 2020 Kyrgyz parliamentary election, Bir Bol received only 3.08% of the vote, losing all 12 seats. The party demanded annulment of the results along with 10 other parties. The election was subsequently annulled by the Central Election Commission.
recent_events.impact: Party lost parliamentary representation; joined the Coordination Council for transfer of power during the October 2020 political crisis.

recent_events.title: Bir Bol Representative Briefly Became Parliament Speaker
recent_events.description: On 6 October 2020, Bir Bol representative Myktybek Abdyldaev became parliament speaker after Dastanbek Dzhumabekov resigned, but resigned himself on 10 October during the ongoing political crisis.
recent_events.impact: Brief but significant moment of parliamentary leadership during a turbulent political transition.

recent_events.title: Dissolved via Merger into Alliance Party
recent_events.description: On 12 October 2021, Bir Bol merged with A Just Kyrgyzstan and the Kyrgyz Liberal Democratic Party to form the Alliance (Альянс) political party. Mirlan Jeenchoroyev became the leader of the new party.
recent_events.impact: Bir Bol ceased to exist as an independent political party after 11 years.

core_business: Liberal political party advocating for state unity, patriotism, administrative-territorial reform, simplified fiscal reporting, educational voucher system, healthcare privatization, and environmental protection. Program centered on five key areas: economy, governance, education, healthcare, and ecology.
apec_stance: As a liberal political party in Kyrgyzstan (an APEC observer economy candidate), Bir Bol advocated for pragmatic economic reforms including simplified fiscal reporting, reduced social fund contributions (from 27.5% to 15%), and creation of a state revenue committee. The party was described by Al Jazeera as pro-Russian (Russophilia), supporting stronger ties with Russia while also promoting liberal economic policies. Kyrgyzstan is not an APEC member economy, so the party had no direct APEC policy stance.

collection_meta.notes: Enriched profile from Russian and English Wikipedia, Wikidata Q21662330. Party was dissolved on 2021-10-12 via merger into Alliance party. Key people identified from multiple sources including 24.kg news archives.
